title: EqMap: FPGA LUT Remapping using E-Graphs
problem: FPGA technology mapping creates a gap between SAT-based exact synthesis and heuristic cut enumeration, resulting in suboptimal LUT counts and circuit depths.
motivation: Decades of research on technology mapping still leaves substantial room for improvement despite understanding the computational complexity.
method: E-graphs are data structures that represent all mathematically equivalent ways to partition a circuit into LUTs (the logic blocks used in FPGAs). The system systematically explores different partitioning strategies by combining exact SAT-based methods—which find provably optimal arrangements—with faster heuristics that guide the search, producing circuits with fewer LUTs and shorter signal paths.
key_novelty: The core contribution is using e-graphs to systematically explore all equivalent FPGA circuit configurations, combining exact optimization methods with practical heuristics to improve LUT mapping.
contributions: 12% average LUT reduction over vendor tools
Reusable compiler infrastructure for RTL equivalence checking and QoR auditing
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific benchmark sets; practical applicability depends on design characteristics.
primary_theme: E-graph compiler for FPGA LUT mapping
